V1.question: Is the NASA data at the pin factual?
V1.truth: Daymet 1 km (temperature); CoCoRaHS gauges (59 stations within 30 km) (rain)
V1.criterion: Tmax and Tmin RMSE <= 2.5 C vs Daymet; May-Sep rain within +-15% of the gauges in >= 80% of years
V1.summary: Tmax RMSE 1.72 C, Tmin RMSE 2.37 C; season rain within 15% in 67% of years against CoCoRaHS gauges (59 stations within 30 km)

V2.question: Would the water model have flagged the bad years?
V2.truth: NASS Story County yields (detrended), USDA RMA insured losses by cause, 2001-2025
V2.criterion: Pearson r >= 0.5 vs detrended yield anomaly and 2012 among the 3 lowest modelled years, per crop (app's POWER rain)
V2.summary: corn FAIL: r=0.03 vs NASS, 2012 flagged, rho=0.61 vs RMA drought; soybean FAIL: r=-0.05 vs NASS, 2012 flagged, rho=0.8 vs RMA drought

V6.question: How much soil does each rotation lose, and how much does a cover crop save?
V6.truth: RUSLE (AH-703) on Daymet rain, SSURGO K and slope length, 3DEP and SSURGO slope; published Iowa figures not yet documented
V6.criterion: The app's erosion score orders the strategies as RUSLE does (higher score = less soil loss)
V6.summary: current 20.13 -> 17.48 t/ha/yr (-13%); small_grain 16.95 -> 14.59 t/ha/yr (-14%); other_family 23.59 -> 20.49 t/ha/yr (-13%) on the 3DEP slope; T = 11.2; score order matches RUSLE

details.blocked: comparison with published Iowa soil-loss figures (source to document)

V8.question: Do the timeline's crop and bare months match what the satellites saw?
V8.truth: Landsat + Sentinel-2 monthly NDVI at the pin (2013-2025) with the CDL crop of each year
V8.criterion: Monthly agreement >= 80% and both season edges within one month in >= 80% of years
V8.summary: 76% of 148 clear months agree; edges within a month in 8% of seasons; a green canopy appears 2.2 months after the FAO-56 planting month on average

V5.question: Do the pest and disease weather rules line up with real losses?
V5.truth: USDA RMA insured losses to plant disease, mycotoxin and insects, NASS Central Iowa district, 2001-2025
V5.criterion: Reported, not scored: Spearman rho with a permutation p-value per rule, and the lead time
V5.summary: no rule reached rho >= 0.4 at p <= 0.05; median lead from the first favourable day to the main loss month 3 months

V3.question: Does the crop evidence point at the crops that thrive here?
V3.truth: CDL crops grown at the pin 2008-2025; NASS Story County (and Iowa) yields
V3.criterion: Corn and soybean ranked above wheat and sunflower; GAEZ attainable yield within +-30% of NASS (2001-2010) for both
V3.summary: GAEZ does not separate the crops (all 10000 at high input); water model ranks Wheat and Sunflower first; attainable vs NASS: Maize 20%, Soybean 99%

V4.question: Is the rotation advice backed by evidence, and how large is the benefit here?
V4.truth: Zhao et al. 2022 meta-analysis, 2112 maize-after-soybean observations; the field's CDL history
V4.criterion: The high-N, Ames-like 95% interval of the soybean pre-crop effect on maize excludes zero
V4.summary: maize after soybean yields 9.9% more than after a non-legume at farm N rates [7.2 to 13.2%], 670 obs; so continuous corn yields 0.91 x rotated corn

V7.question: Would choosing by expected margin have paid, and could the farm plant on time?
V7.truth: NASS Story County yields, NASS Iowa prices received and days suitable for fieldwork; placeholder costs
V7.criterion: The margin rule's realised margin 2008-2025 is at least the farmer's (strict alternation)
V7.summary: margin rule $11995 vs farmer $12250 vs continuous corn $10366 vs hindsight $13567 per ha over 18 years; differs from the farmer in 8 years; short of planting days in 0 of 25 springs
